paragraphs: Vekevan deballayla hu shelitat haddinim lekak nitqan lomar pasuq vehu rachum qodem qeriat shema ubirkoteha ditpillat arbit bechol davqa, ukemo shekkatab rabbenu za"l beseper peri etz chayyim vezeh leshono: "vehu rachum" shebbitpillat arbit yesh y"g tibben keneged y"g mekilin daarik anpin, leakpiy kullehu dinin ulematteq bahem d' partzupin diqlippa hammatchilin lehitorer bearbit vehem mashchit aon ap vechema veku', vegam lekavven shhqb"h merachem al hareshaim begehinnam sheaz tippin esh yoredin begehinnam vehem "par" vshk"h manni dinin, vetzarik lematteqan, vetob lekavven rashe tebot "vehu rachum yekapper" ry"v keminyan gebura verashe tebot "rachum yekapper aon" mispar "par" ad kan dabrin, yeuyyan sham, velaken en omerim pasuq vehu rachum ella raq bechol, abal bearbit deshabbat asur lomar pasuq zeh kan, mihu omerim oto beshabbat bizmirot, veraq kan shennitqan bishbil shelitat haddinim asur leomero beshabbat, ki beshabbat en shelitat haddinim ukemo shekkatub bazzohar haqqadosh teruma dap ql"h ammud b', veasur leamma qaddisha lemiptach legabbah pesuqa dedina kegon vehu rachum veku' yeuyyan sham ukemo shekkatab haggaon chida" za"l behaggahotayv sham yeuyyan sham, umikkan atta lamed sheggam keshechal yom hakkippurim bechol gam ken en lomar pasuq zeh shel vehu rachum vekaasher niktob zeh bimqomo:

clarification.explanation: Since the forces of judgment (din) hold sway at night, it was instituted to say the verse "Vehu Rachum" before the Shema and its blessings in the evening prayer — but only on weekdays. The Ari, of blessed memory, explains that the verse "Vehu Rachum" contains thirteen words corresponding to the Thirteen Attributes of "Arich Anpin" (supernal mercy), whose function is to subdue the forces of judgment and sweeten the four "faces" of the kelipah that begin to stir in the evening. There is also an intention here that the Holy One, blessed be He, has mercy on the wicked in Gehinnom, when drops of fire called "par" (corresponding to 365 kinds of judgments) descend there, requiring sweetening; and it is also good to have in mind that the initial letters of "Vehu Rachum Yechaper" add up to 216 ("Rei\"v"), the numerical value of "Gevurah," and the initial letters of "Rachum Yechaper Avon" add up to the value of "par." Therefore the verse "Vehu Rachum" is said only on weekdays; but in the evening prayer of Shabbat it is forbidden to say it here (although it is said on Shabbat during the Zemirot), because on Shabbat there is no dominion of judgment, and it is forbidden for the "holy nation" to open with verses of judgment on Shabbat. From this we learn that even when Yom Kippur falls on a weekday, the verse "Vehu Rachum" should not be said.
takeaways: Say the verse "Vehu Rachum" before the Shema of the evening prayer — only on weekdays, not on Shabbat.

Accompanying intentions: God's mercy on the wicked in Gehinnom (fiery drops called "par" requiring sweetening), and the gematria of the initial letters — "Vehu Rachum Yechaper" = 216, the value of Gevurah; "Rachum Yechaper Avon" = the value of "par."

paragraphs: Achar pasuq vehu rachum omerim shelosha pesuqim "Adonai tzebaot immanu veku'" "Adonai tzebaot ashre adam boteach bak", "Adonai hoshia veku'" vekamporash beshaar hakkavvanot yeuyyan sham, vekatab mhr" hakkohen za"l beshem harama"q za"l depasuq ' amaro abraham abinu alayv hashshalom, upasuq sheni amaro yitzchaq abinu alayv hashshalom, upasuq shelishi amaro yaaqob abinu alayv hashshalom, laken rashe tebot yaanenu beyom qaraenu im ayi"n shel yaanenu hem otiyyot yaaqob, vehinneh poh irenu bagdad y" nohagim lomar techilla poseq ki el rachum Adonai eloheka lo yarpeka veku' hakkatub beparashat vaetchannan, veacharayv omerim vehu rachum yekapper aon veacharayv g' pesuqim hannizkarim, veacharehem omerim vibareku sham kebodeka umeromam al kol beraka utehilla veomer qaddish velo bittalnu minhagam bishne pesuqim shel el rachum veshel vibareku, ki amarnu "p sheen lahem shoresh kepi hassod en qepida leomeram shello matzinu lerabbenu haari"y za"l shehiqpid kan ella baamirat hammizmorim:

clarification.explanation: After the verse "Vehu Rachum," one says three verses: "Hashem Tzeva'ot imanu...," "Hashem Tzeva'ot, ashrei adam boteach bach," and "Hashem hoshi'ah..." It is received in the name of the Kabbalists that each verse belongs to one of the Patriarchs: the first to Avraham, the second to Yitzchak, the third to Yaakov — and the initial letters at the end of the third verse ("Ya'aneinu beyom kor'einu") allude to the name "Yaakov." In Baghdad the custom developed to add, before all this, the verse "Ki Kel rachum Hashem Elokecha" (from Parashat Va'etchanan), followed by "Vehu Rachum yechaper avon," followed by the three verses mentioned, and afterward "Vivarchu shem kevodecha" and Kaddish. Although these additions ("Ki Kel Rachum" and "Vivarchu") have no explicit source in the teachings of the Kabbalah, there is no reason to refrain from saying them, since the Ari, of blessed memory, was particular about this matter only regarding the recitation of the Psalms.
takeaways: The order of verses after "Vehu Rachum": three verses belonging to Avraham, Yitzchak, and Yaakov.
The custom of Baghdad adds two more verses before and after — and there is nothing wrong with this, even though they have no explicit source in the Kabbalah.

paragraphs: Keshemmatchil birkat asher bidbaro maarib yisgor enayv veyachaboq yadayv im hu mitpallel beal peh, veyesh taam al pi hassod lisgirat haenayim biqriat shema ubirkoteha dearbit, umihu kol zeh bechol, abal bearbit deshabbat veyom tob lo yisgor enayv biqriat shema ubirkoteha:

clarification.explanation: When one begins the blessing "Asher bidvaro ma'ariv aravim," he should close his eyes and clasp his hands, if he is praying by heart. There is a reason, according to the Kabbalah, for closing the eyes during the Shema and its blessings in the evening prayer, but all this applies only on weekdays; on the evening prayer of Shabbat and Yom Tov, one should not close his eyes during the Shema and its blessings.
takeaways: On weekday evenings — close the eyes and clasp the hands during the blessing "Asher bidvaro ma'ariv aravim" (if praying by heart).
On the evening prayer of Shabbat and Yom Tov — do not close the eyes during the Shema and its blessings.

paragraphs: Pesuqe haddebarim shel beraka harishona hu kak maarib arabim bechakema, veaach"k poteach shearim bitbuna, veyasim rivvach benehem kede sheyyihyeh nishma bechakema al maarib arabim, vetebat bitbuna al poteach shearim, veaach"k yomar meshanneh ittim veku' baraqia kirtzono, veyasim rivvach veaach"k yomar bore yomam valayla ki tebat kirtzono qae addilel, veenah mequshsheret im bore yomam valayla vekannizkar beshaar hakkavvanot:

clarification.explanation: One must pay attention to the correct division of words in the first blessing of the evening prayer: one says "Ma'ariv aravim bechochmah," and afterward "Poteach she'arim bitvunah," with a slight pause between them, so that it will be heard that "bechochmah" refers to "Ma'ariv aravim" and "bitvunah" refers to "Poteach she'arim." And afterward one says "Meshaneh itim... barakia kirtzono," with a pause, and afterward "Borei yomam valailah" — because the word "kirtzono" refers to what precedes it, and is not connected to "Borei yomam valailah."
takeaways: One should pause slightly between the phrases in the first blessing of the evening prayer, so that each description attaches to the correct word ("bechochmah" to "Ma'ariv aravim," "bitvunah" to "Poteach she'arim," and "kirtzono" to what precedes "Borei yomam valailah," not to it).

paragraphs: En lehapsiq ben berakot dearbit litpilla ki im baamirat hashkibenu vaaniyyat qaddish vachamishsha ummanim deqaddish vetu la middi, ubemah shemmakriz hachazzan rosh chodesh ben qaddish litpilla yesh lepaqpeq, ak bemaqom shennahagu lehakriz en limchot beyadam, gam amen dibraka deshomer et ammo yisrael lo yaaneh ki zeh amen dibrakot hu, veen onin kan ummanim dibrakot:

clarification.explanation: One may not interrupt between the blessings of the evening prayer and the Amidah, except for saying "Hashkiveinu," answering Kaddish, and the five "amens" within it — and nothing more. The chazzan's announcement of Rosh Chodesh between the Kaddish and the Amidah is subject to doubt, but where the custom is to announce it, one should not protest against those who do. Likewise, one should not answer "amen" to the blessing "Shomer et amo Yisrael" — because this blessing is adjacent to the one before it, and one does not answer "amen" to a blessing that is adjacent to another.
takeaways: Do not interrupt between the blessings of the evening prayer and the Amidah — except for "Hashkiveinu," Kaddish, and the five amens within it.
Do not answer "amen" to the blessing "Shomer et amo Yisrael."

paragraphs: Achar tepillat arbit omer hashlicha tzibbur qaddish titqabbel veshir lemaalot veacharayv qaddish yehe shelama ubareku, vekatabti leel beparashat ki tissa depoh irenu nohagim lomar kan rabbanan bareku et Adonai hamborak shemmosipin lomar rabbanan veaach"k alenu leshabbeach bekavvana gedola, venohagim poh irenu lomar achar alenu leshabbeach vidduy umizmor shir hammaalot beshub Adonai et shibat tziyyon veacharayv qaddish, abal beir haqqodesh tvb"b lo nahagu lomar vidduy velo hammizmor hannizkar, vekimdummeh li sheshshamati taam leminhag havvidduy poh irenu kan hu bimqom vidduy deomerim al hammitta, vekatabti leharab haggaon mhr" minni nr"v lehodieni minhag are haqqodesh ttvb"b vekatab li dibir haqqodesh chebron tvb"b nohagim lomar achar arbit vidduy veshir hammaalot beshub Adonai et shibat tziyyon veqaddish vehu shama sham shezzeh hamminhag nityassed sham "p rab shebba meir shealuneqi vehaya sham choleim gedolim umita pitomit, vechalam tzaddiq echad sheyyetaqqenu vidduy achar arbit vetitbattel haggezera, veken asu venitbattela, umeoto zeman nohagim ken beshealuneqi y" ubeboo leir haqqodesh chebron t"v hinhig otam bekak, ubearbit sheen bah vidduy omerim shir hammaalot bilbad veqaddish, umerosh chodesh elul ad shemini atzeret omerim achar shacharit vearbit mizmor ori veyishi veacharayv qaddish ad kan debarayv nr"v:

clarification.explanation: After the evening prayer, the chazzan says Kaddish "Titkabel" and "Shir Lama'alot," and after it Kaddish "Yehei Shelama" and "Barchu." In Baghdad the custom is to add the word "Rabbanan" before "Barchu et Hashem hamevorach," and afterward "Aleinu leshabe'ach" with great intention. Likewise, in Baghdad the custom is to say, after "Aleinu leshabe'ach," a confession (Vidui) and the psalm "Shir Hama'alot, beshuv Hashem et shivat Tzion," and after it Kaddish — but in Jerusalem this was not the custom. The source of the custom of the Vidui here appears to be as a substitute for the Vidui said upon retiring to bed. Inquiry made with a rabbi from Hebron revealed that there too the custom is to say this Vidui and psalm after the evening prayer — and that this custom began in Salonika, after a certain tzaddik dreamed, during a severe epidemic, that they should institute a Vidui after the evening prayer and the decree would be annulled, and so it was. From Rosh Chodesh Elul until Shemini Atzeret, one adds after Shacharit and Ma'ariv the psalm "LeDavid, Hashem ori veyish'i," followed by Kaddish.
takeaways: The order after the evening prayer: Kaddish Titkabel, Shir Lama'alot, Kaddish Yehei Shelama, Barchu, Aleinu leshabe'ach.
The custom of Baghdad and Hebron: to add a Vidui and the psalm "Shir Hama'alot beshuv Hashem" after Aleinu leshabe'ach.
From Rosh Chodesh Elul until Shemini Atzeret, one adds after Shacharit and Ma'ariv the psalm "LeDavid Hashem ori veyish'i."

paragraphs: En liqro miqra ballelot shel chol, vehattaam dehammiqra baasiyya vehallayla bechinat asiyya vehakkol hu dinin veen leorer haddinin ukemo shekkatab rabbenu za"l beshaar hammitzot parashat vaetchannan ayyen sham, mihu belel shabbat velel yom tob qorin miqra veen lachush, veken belel shishshi qorin k"v pesuqim veen chashash, abal lel rosh chodesh dino beinyan zeh kishar lelot hachol, vehaggaon chida" za"l bahashmatot seper "petach enayim" katab deam haaretz sheeno yodea liqrot ella raq tora shebbiktab shari liqrot ballayla ayyen sham, mihu nireh im yodea liqrot pereq ezehu meqoman o petichat eliyyahu zakur lattob sheyyesh bassiddurim beashshurit umenuqqadim, yiqra otam veyachazor otam kamma peamim vezeh adip milliqro miqra: vekatab haggaon chida" za"l sheshshama meadam gadol umequbbal deyesh lechalleq ben qeriat tehillim lishar hammiqra ayyen sham, veyesh lismok al debarayv biqriat tehillim achar chatzot layla davqa veim qore hammiqra bilshonot acherim kede lehitlammed beur hammiqra beoto lashon peshita deshare ukemo shekkatab hakkeneset haggedola dibtargum lo shayyak lomar debarim shebbiktab i epshar leomeram beal peh, veayyen leharab birke yosep siman m"t seip qatan ' vechiqre leb orach chayyim siman y"b:

clarification.explanation: One should not read Tanach on weekday nights, because reading belongs to the realm of Asiyah (Action), and night, too, is in the aspect of Asiyah — a domain where judgment holds sway, and one should not arouse it. But on Shabbat night and Yom Tov night it is permitted to read Scripture, and likewise on Friday night (when the custom is to read twenty-six verses). The night of Rosh Chodesh has the same status as other weekday nights, and is forbidden. One who can read only the Written Torah is permitted to read it at night. And one who knows how to recite the chapter "Eizehu Mekoman" or "Petichat Eliyahu," it is preferable that he recite and repeat these several times, rather than read ordinary Scripture. There is a distinction between reciting Psalms and other Scripture, and one may rely on this to permit reciting Psalms after midnight specifically. Reading Scripture in translation into another language, for the purpose of learning its meaning, is permitted, since with a translation into another language there is no problem of "words given in writing may not be recited by heart."
takeaways: Do not read Tanach on weekday nights (except Shabbat night, Yom Tov night, and Friday night) — because night is a time when judgment holds sway.
It is permitted to recite "Eizehu Mekoman" or "Petichat Eliyahu" at night, and Psalms after midnight; and it is permitted to read Scripture in translation for the purpose of study.

paragraphs: Hashshena laadam ballayla yesh bah tzorek vetoelet gam mitztzad haruchaniyyut, mippene sheyyesh bah sod shehahi tzorek gabohha, velaken tzarik haadam lekavven sheggam beet hashshena hu obed et boreo besod bekol derakeka daehu, velaken tiqqenu rabbotenu za"l beraka al hashshena vehi birkat hammappil, ak hashshena beyom raa latztzaddiqim vetoba lareshaim, millebad beyom hashshabbat shehashshena hi toba gam latztzaddiqim vekannizkar beshaar hakkavvanot:

clarification.explanation: Sleep at night has a need and a benefit even from the spiritual side, for it contains a lofty secret; therefore a person should intend that even while sleeping he is serving his Creator — in the aspect of "Know Him in all your ways." Therefore the Sages instituted a special blessing over sleep, the blessing of "Hamapil." But sleeping during the day is bad for the righteous and good for the wicked, except on the day of Shabbat, when sleep is good for everyone.
takeaways: Sleep at night, too, is service of God, and therefore a special blessing was instituted over it (the blessing of Hamapil).
Sleeping during the day — bad for the righteous, good for the wicked, except on Shabbat, when sleep is good for everyone.

paragraphs: Tob lehizzaher shello yashan ballayla ella ad sheyyaabru shelosha shaot min hallayla veyesh sod baddabar kede lehaamid orot hammochin haelyonim kannizkar beshaar hakkavvanot, vekatabti besipri haqqatan mqbtzyl deshiur shelosha shaot hannizkar matchilim mittepillat arbit, sheim hitpallel arbit mibbeod yom dehaynu biplag hammincha ledaat rabbi yehuda yachshob hashshalosh shaot meoto zeman:

clarification.explanation: It is good to be careful not to sleep at night until three hours have passed from the start of the night, and there is a secret in this, in order to establish the lights of the supernal intellects. These three hours are counted from the time of the evening prayer — so that one who prayed the evening prayer while it was still day, at "Plag HaMinchah" (according to the opinion of Rabbi Yehudah), counts the three hours from that earlier time.
takeaways: Try not to sleep until three hours have passed from the evening prayer (or from Plag HaMinchah, if one prayed early).

paragraphs: Bitchillat hallayla yishkab haadam al tzad semol davqa, veachar chatzot layla im yirtzeh yithappek al tzad yemino, uminhag zeh moil lo lebattel kochot hachitzonim ukemo shekkatub beshaar hakkavvanot, veyizzaher sheyyashen betallit qatan shello yipshot oto gam beshekkabu ballayla al mittato, veyoil zeh meod lebattel kochot hachitzonim vekannizkar beshaar hakkavvanot, veyizzaher gam ken shello yihyeh alayv barzel kesheyyashen, veyizzaher shello yazkir bepiv shem semek-mem apillu bayyom vekol shekken ballayla sheaz hu zeman shallitato, veshem shemot hashshedim sheyyesh bilshon laaz lo yazkir haadam bepiv, sheggam hashshedim hem bechelqo shel semek-mem umagbir koach kaasher zokerim otam vekannizkar beshaar hakkavvanot:

clarification.explanation: At the beginning of the night, one should lie specifically on the left side, and after midnight one may turn onto the right side. This practice helps to nullify the external forces (kelipot). One must be careful to sleep while wearing a tallit katan, without removing it even while lying down at night, which also greatly helps to nullify those forces. One must also be careful not to have iron on him while sleeping, and not to say with his mouth the name "Samech-Mem" (a name for Satan), even during the day, and certainly not at night when it is his time of dominion; and one should likewise not mention with his mouth the names of demons given in foreign languages, since demons too belong to the portion of "Samech-Mem," and mentioning their name increases their power.
takeaways: Lie on the left side at the start of the night, and turn to the right side after midnight.
Sleep wearing a tallit katan, without iron on the body, and avoid saying the name of Satan or the names of demons aloud.

paragraphs: Tzarik lehizzaher meod biqriat shema sheal hammitta, vehi achat min arbaa qeriat shema shechayyab adam bekol yom vehi haqqetanna shebbahem bemadregot, ulemala mimmenna qeriat shema dearbit, ulemala mimmenna qeriat shema deqarebbanot, ulemala mikkullam qeriat shema deyotzer vekaasher bearnu leel (parashat vaere, ot b'), veda aqa, shebbeet shehu qore qeriat shema al hammitta al harob hashshena ben enayv, veikka lemichash pen yibla tebot veotiyyot, velaken tzarik tigboret gedola baet hahi lehitazzer veliqrotah karauy, veseder qeriat shema zo im kol happesuqim hashshayyakim lah nitpareshu bedibre rabbenu haari"y za"l beshaar hakkavvanot venidpesu bassiddurim vehem yeduim lekol veen tzorek lehaatiqam poh, ubeamero pasuq beyadeka apqid ruchi, paditta oti Adonai el emet yekavven beyadeka apqid ruchi rashe tebot beer, veken yekavven br"t padita oti Adonai shem p"y, vehu rashe tebot "poteach et yadeka" sheoleh missipro shem yhdvnh"y veshem saa"l, haramuz berashe tebot "atta satar li", viharher bappasuq hazzeh uberashe tebot shello ad sheyyashen, veam haaretz sheeno yodea lomar happesuqim, veken ishsha sheenah yodaat, yomru bepihem otiyyot lp" byt" dbg"d, o "baruk Adonai leolam amen veamen", kamma peamim bezo achar zo, ad sheyyeshno mittok dibre tora: veda ki bassiddurim katub lomar hashkibenu abinu leshalom veku' ak beshaar hakkavvanot lo hizkir hashkibenu, amenam besiddur rabbenu harasha"sh za"l hizkir zeh, vezehu hasseder shekkatub besiddur rabbenu harasha"sh za"l birkat hammappil vehashkibenu uqeriat shema, veaach"k yalezu chasidim veku' veaach"k hinneh mittato shelosh peamim veaach"k "yebarekka veku'" "yaer veku'" "yissa veku'", veaach"k "yosheb beseter" ad "Adonai machasi", veaach"k vidduy veaach"k "anna bekoach" kullah vechozer pasuq shekkeneged oto hayyom shelosh peamim, veaach"k "atta taqum terachem tziyyon veku'" veaach"k "beyadeka apqid ruchi veku'" vekavvanat shem elohha:

clarification.explanation: One must be very careful with the Shema recited upon the bed — it is one of the four recitations of the Shema that a person is obligated in every day, and it is the lowest of them in rank (above it is the Shema of the evening prayer, above that the Shema of the Korbanot, and above all of them the Shema of Yotzer, as explained above in Parashat Vaera). The problem is that at the time one recites the Shema upon the bed, sleep is generally already overtaking him, and there is concern lest he swallow words and letters — therefore one must make a great effort to strengthen himself and recite it properly. The exact order of the verses is found in the words of the Ari, of blessed memory, in Sha'ar HaKavanot, and is printed in the prayer books, so there is no need to copy it here. When saying the verse "Beyadecha afkid ruchi, paditah oti Hashem Kel emet," one should have in mind that the initial letters of "Beyadecha afkid ruchi" spell "Be'er," and the initial letters of "Paditah oti Hashem" spell "Pa\"y" — which are the initial letters of "Poteach et yadecha," whose numerical value equals the Name Havayah [spelled out] and the Name Sa'al, alluded to in "Atah seter li" — and to meditate on this verse and these initial letters until falling asleep. An unlearned person who does not know the verses, and likewise a woman who does not know them, should say the letters of the alphabet, or "Baruch Hashem le'olam" repeatedly, until they fall asleep amid words of Torah. In the prayer books it says to recite "Hashkiveinu" before this Shema, though in Sha'ar HaKavanot this is not mentioned; but in the prayer book of the Rashash it is mentioned, and according to it the order is: the blessing of Hamapil, Hashkiveinu, the Shema, "Ya'alzu chasidim," "Hineh mitato" three times, the Priestly Blessing (Yevarechecha, Ya'er, Yisa), the psalm "Yoshev beseter," Vidui, "Ana beko'ach" in full with a threefold repetition of the verse suited to that day, and afterward "Atah takum terachem Tzion" and "Beyadecha afkid ruchi."
takeaways: The Shema recited upon the bed requires special attention, because sleep begins to overtake one at the time of its recitation.

The intention of the initial letters in the verse "Beyadecha afkid ruchi, paditah oti Hashem": "Be'er" and "Pa\"y" (= "Poteach et yadecha," equal to the Name Havayah and the Name Sa'al, alluded to in "Atah seter li").
One who does not know the verses (an unlearned person or a woman) should say the alphabet or "Baruch Hashem le'olam" repeatedly.
There is a detailed order of verses surrounding this Shema according to the prayer book of the Rashash.

paragraphs: Birkat hammappil nitqena beshem umalkut veken tzarik lemor kepi dibre rabbenu haari"y za"l, ak yesh nohagim sheen mebarekim otah beshem umalkut veken minhagi uminhag adoni abi za"l, vehattaam mippene hachashash shemma yihyeh mukrach lehapsiq beezeh debarim sheyyihyeh mukrach ledabber bam, vekatabti lididenu harab haggaon mhr" minni nr"v lehodieni minhag hachasidim beare haqqodesh tvb"b, vekatab li deharob enam mebarekim beshem umalkut, od katab sheraa biktab rabbi abraham lzrqy za"l shekkatab raiti gedolim beyisrael sheenam mebarekim beraka zo, mittaam shemma yitztareku lehapsiq bedibbur, veyesh kamma poseqim disbira lehu sheim pasaq have beraka lebattala veayyen petach haddebir cheleq b' si' rl"t, ad kan debarayv nr"v. al ken nireh lehorot shekkol echad yaaseh keminhago bazeh veazhara gedola lehambarekim sheyyishtaddelu meod laamod al atzmam shello lehapsiq bedibbur ben beraka leshena heka shello baa lahem hashshena tekep, vegam hachoshesh veeno mebarek beshem umalkut yizzaher leharher shem umalkut belibbo: gam da ki matzati katub beseper keter malkut ketibat yad lomar techillat hakkol qodem hammappil "leshem yichud qudesha berik hu ushekinatah veku', harenu meqabbel elohuto yitbarek veahabato veyirato, vahareni yare mimmennu begin deihu rab veshallit al kolla vekulla qammeh kelo, vahareni mimmeliku al kol eber veeber gid vegid mimmatayim ushemona vearbaim ebarim veshalosh meot vachamishsha veshishshim gidim shel gupe venapshi ruchi venishme malkut gemura ushelema, vahareni ebed lehashshem yitbarek vehu berachamayv yezakkenu leabedo belebab shalem venepesh chapetza amen ken yehi ratzon" - ad kan leshono, vekak ani noheg:

clarification.explanation: The blessing of "Hamapil" was instituted with Name and Kingship, and so it should be said, according to the Ari, of blessed memory. But there are those who have the custom not to say it with Name and Kingship — and this is also the custom of Rabbi Yosef Chaim and the custom of his father — out of concern that he might have to interrupt with speech before falling asleep (for example, if sleep is delayed). The custom of most of the pious in the holy cities is likewise not to say it with Name and Kingship, out of the same concern about interrupting with speech, since some hold that such an interruption may turn the blessing into a blessing said in vain. Rabbi Yosef Chaim's ruling: each person should follow his own custom, but those who do say it with Name and Kingship must be very careful not to interrupt with speech between the blessing and sleep if sleep is delayed; and one who is concerned and does not say it with Name and Kingship should meditate on Name and Kingship in his heart. There is also a formula (found in the book Keter Malchut) to say before Hamapil: "Leshem yichud Kudsha Berich Hu uShechinteih," in which a person accepts God's kingship over all his limbs and sinews and declares himself a servant of God — and this is Rabbi Yosef Chaim's practice.
takeaways: The blessing of "Hamapil": some have the custom to say it with Name and Kingship, and some do not — out of concern about interrupting with speech before sleep; each person should follow his own custom.
It is good to say before the blessing of Hamapil the formula "Leshem yichud" from the book Keter Malchut.

paragraphs: Biqriat shema zo sheal hammitta yekavven letaqqen aon qeri veshikbat zera lebattala sheyyatza mimmennu ben beshogeg ben bemezid, sheyyamutu haggupim hattomeim hammalbishim lanneshamot shennesheqa otam hassitra achara mikkoach otam tippot shel zera sheyyatzeu mimmennu lebattala, veyachzeru otam hanneshamot haqqedoshot liqdushsha veyabou baolam hazzeh kishar kol neshamot haqqedoshot, vetoil qeriat shema bekavvana zo gam leotan tippot zera sheyyetzeu mimmennu achar sheshshimmesh mittato shello shaha al habbeten ad sheyyetzeu mimmennu kol hattippin kullam, vegam lerabbot otam tippin qetannim sheyyatzeu mimmennu lipamim al yede itztzur sheddocheq atzmo baasiyyat tzerakayv, vegam lerabbot tippin qetannim sheyyatzeu mimmennu "y qishshuy haeber qodem tashmish, sheadayin lo niknas hashshemesh bimqomo mechamat ezeh ikkub shehaya lo hen bauna hen beratzon, uqeriat shema zo toil gam leishsha baabur zera hayyotze mimmenna mechamat ribbuy taava shemmitoreret bah, sheal zeh neemar venega lo yiqrab beaholeka zo ishteka shenniqret ohel veayyen beseper hakkavvanot:

clarification.explanation: In this Shema recited upon the bed, one should have in mind to rectify the sin of seminal emission (keri), whether inadvertent or intentional — so that the impure bodies clothing the souls seized by the Sitra Achra through those wasted drops should die, and those holy souls return to holiness and come into this world like other holy souls. This rectification also helps for drops of seed that emerge after marital relations, when one did not remain lying on the stomach until all the drops came out, and for small drops that emerge from straining during bodily needs, and for drops that emerge from arousal before relations. This Shema also benefits a woman, regarding seed that emerges from her due to increased desire.
takeaways: The Shema recited upon the bed also rectifies the sin of seminal emission, whether inadvertent or intentional, and similar matters relating to seed improperly emitted, for both men and women.

paragraphs: Im osin tiqqun karet shenneorin kol hallayla kemo lel shebuot vehoshana rabba, yomru haqriat shema sheal hammitta meat qodem chatzot im kol happesuqim shel yalezu veku' hinneh veku' yebarekka veku' yosheb basseter veku' ana bekoach veku':

clarification.explanation: One who performs a "tikkun" of remaining awake all night, such as on the night of Shavuot or Hoshana Rabbah, should recite the Shema upon the bed a little before midnight, together with all its accompanying verses ("Ya'alzu chasidim," "Hineh," the Priestly Blessing, "Yoshev beseter," "Ana beko'ach," etc.).
takeaways: On nights of "tikkun" (Shavuot, Hoshana Rabbah) — recite the Shema upon the bed a little before midnight, not at the end of the night.

paragraphs: En okelim veshotim velo medabberim achar qeriat shema sheal hammitta, veim qara veeno yakol lishon kebar katabnu leel sheyyitammetz laamod al atzmo leharher bedibre tora kede sheyyashen mittok dibre tora, veyashbia atzmo middibre tora hannotenet chayyim leoseh umotzeah matza chayyim:

clarification.explanation: After the Shema recited upon the bed, one should not eat, drink, or speak. One who recited it and cannot fall asleep should, as already written above, exert himself to meditate on words of Torah so that he falls asleep amid Torah study.
takeaways: After the Shema upon the bed — do not eat, drink, or speak; one who cannot fall asleep should meditate on words of Torah until he does.
